Even if we assume that Russia stole and released the e-mails Wikilinks published, they didn't do anything to the election. I keep seeing this in headlines, that Russia hacked the election. The implication of that wording is that they actually did something to directly effect the outcome, which just wouldn't be the case.

I'm not trying to go with the 'they just revealed the truth' line. It may be true, but I doubt there is a public official who would look good at that point (things said in private don't play well in public, think of Trump's Hollywood Access bus ordeal) and let's face it, most people didn't read any of them and think that everything the Wikilinks e-mails revealed is just some nutty conspiracy theory. What I am saying is that the release of the e-mails is not an affront to our democracy or any of the other outrageous claims being made now, it's muckraking. That's it, it's muckraking. It's not a good thing, never really has been. But it has been with our democracy for as long as our democracy has existed.

Nothing has changed and nothing has been damaged. I would figure that Putin would have more important things to do than make meme magic easier, but even if he was bored and just figured the Chans needed more post fodder, Russia did not "hack the election".
Even if Russia was actually behind the e-mail hacks, they didn't "hack the election".
